title: Introduce subscriber-window peeking and correlation-aware fingerprint for canary detector
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: previous canary fingerprinting treated subscribers independently which produced false positives when short-lived cross-subscriber latency bursts occurred concurrently. This PR adds a correlation-aware fingerprint that factors cross-subscriber covariation and a lightweight peeking buffer so detectors can align windows across moving subscriber streams. Goals: reduce false positives for multi-tenant workloads, surface correlated degradations, and provide a gradual rollout path with safe fallback. Design summary: 1) subscriber window peeking: a bounded in-memory sliding window per logical subscriber that exposes aligned windows to aggregators; peeking is read-only to avoid changing request ordering. 2) correlation fingerprint: compute pairwise Pearson covariances on aggregated latency summaries and compress into a fixed-length correlation fingerprint used by the canary classifier. 3) scoring: detector now combines single-subscriber anomaly score and correlation anomaly score with a tunable weight canary.detectors.correlation_weight. 4) safety: feature gated behind canary.detectors.correlation_enabled default false, with fast fallback to legacy fingerprint when correlation module is disabled or OOM is detected. Implementation notes: added a new stream stage subscriber_peek_buffer, implemented correlation_fingerprint module with single-pass incremental covariance estimator to keep memory bounded, added config schema bump v1.13 for the two new properties, added short-circuit paths to ensure sub-ms added latency for normal traffic. Tests and verification: unit tests for covariance estimator and peeking buffer, integration test that injects synchronized latency spikes across three subscribers and asserts reduction in false positive rate compared to legacy detector, e2e perf bench that measures overhead across 1000 concurrent subscribers. Observability and alerts: new metrics canary.correlation_coeff_avg, canary.cross_subscriber_cov_max, canary.correlation_faults_total; dashboard tile added to perf-canary Grafana (grafana/dashboards/correlation.json) and alert rule canary-high-correlation that triggers at correlation_coeff_avg > 0.6 during canaries. Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag and config default false, stage 1 deploy to canary cluster with smoke tests, stage 2 limited traffic rollout to 10% customers with auto rollback if perf-regression-check fails, stage 3 enable by default with monitoring for one week. Related: ENG-4820 covers detector design, ENG-4901 tracks rollout telemetry requirements, SUP-9821 motivated by a customer incident where co-located subscribers caused noisy canary spikes. Backwards compatibility: config bump is additive and safe. Performance impact: negligible steady-state memory and CPU overhead; worst-case when correlation window length is large can cause extra work but bounded by configured window_ms and max_pairs. Why unique: instead of just changing thresholds or window sizes this PR adds cross-subscriber signal awareness which reduces correlated false positives that previous PRs did not address.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Overall looks good. Please confirm worst-case memory growth and add a defensive cap on pair tracking. Also suggest lowering default correlation_weight to 0.2 until we have more field data.

Asha Patel: Added pair cap of 250 pairs and set default correlation_weight to 0.2, documented rationale in docs/perf-canary/correlation.md. Measured memory bump at 250 pairs is ~1.2MB per detector instance in our test harness.
Ellen Park: Integration test is valuable but flaked once on CI due to timing assumptions. Can we make the injector deterministic or add retry logic?
Asha Patel: Updated integration test to use simulated clock and added retry-based assert to reduce flakiness. Also annotated test with @flaky to assist CI triage if it still flakes.
ci_checks: e2e-perf: pass (bench numbers within 1.5% of baseline)
release_notes: Add optional correlation-aware canary fingerprint to reduce false positives from synchronized subscriber spikes. Feature is disabled by default and can be enabled via canary.detectors.correlation_enabled. Configurable window and weight parameters added. Safe fallback to legacy fingerprint provided.
